checks.finding: The closed views show one base, one lid, four lid screw heads, one UART opening and two cable-tie slots.
The 78 by 88 mm case encloses the native 60 by 70 mm carrier. The open views show the 21 by 51 mm Pico above its two specified socket and header rows.
The top UART opening aligns with the three carrier pins. The open top shows the USB receptacle facing the open-top wall notch; both strain-relief slots are visible in the lid.
The native Pico components remain on the board, the two header rows seat over the carrier sockets, and the visible mounting hardware belongs to the four carrier and four perimeter mounting sites.
The interior view shows four carrier screws, four tall lid standoffs, and the Pico supported on two socket rows. The closed lid seats on the perimeter standoffs.

The native USB faces +Y and the populated side faces +Z. The top view places the native LED on the pin-1 side, to the left of USB. The source independently checks this asymmetric LED and both native pad rows.
Closed and open top/iso views agree on the single case, left UART opening, centred USB notch, socket stack and perimeter mounting hardware.

findings: Reviewed actual OCCT renders of the exact corrected source in closed and interior top/iso views.
The native Pico uses a proper Rx(90) rotation and translation. Its 17 manufacturer solids retain their original shape and handedness.
Three native carrier gauges, three native Pico gauges and the asymmetric native LED witness distinguish physical pin-1 orientation from a symmetric but incorrect row swap.
Printed tolerances, soldered stack height, real cable overmolds and physical assembly remain unqualified.
